channel.title: Julio Cesar Mauro — Writing
channel.description: Security and infrastructure articles by Julio Cesar Mauro.

item.title: BootROM Leak: The Key 95 Million PS5s Can't Replace
item.description: What actually leaked when PS5 BootROM key material surfaced online at the end of 2025 — why a key burned into silicon can't be patched like a kernel bug, and why most of the panic around it got ahead of the evidence.

item.title: Relapse: The Browser Bug That Opened the PS5's Kernel
item.description: How the Relapse jailbreak chains a JavaScriptCore memory corruption bug with a kernel use-after-free race in aiomultiwait — and why every major public PS5 kernel exploit since 2022 traces back to FreeBSD, not Sony's own code.

item.title: PHP2Shell: 72 Hours of Internet-Wide Panic
item.description: How two critical pre-auth RCE bugs in PHP's engine itself (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) turned into days of scrambled advisories, conflicting mitigations and honeypot-confirmed scanning across the internet.

item.title: Your Container's Identity Is Worth More Than Root
item.description: How a non-root container with limited file read access becomes the pivot point for cross-account IAM escalation via the metadata endpoint and image layer history.

item.title: One Wildcard in a Trust Policy
item.description: How StringLike with a glob pattern in an IAM trust policy condition turns a controlled role assumption into an open path — and why StringEquals matters.

item.title: The Header That Opened the Network
item.description: Why X-Forwarded-For should never be used for access control at the edge — and how one misconfigured Nginx directive led to full internal network access.

item.title: systemd as an Attack Surface
item.description: How services running as root that source files from user-influenced paths enable privilege escalation without a CVE — just a timer and a writable directory.

item.title: RBAC: When No Single Permission Seems Critical
item.description: How create Jobs combined with a permissive service account enables namespace lateral movement — and why Kubernetes RBAC must be reviewed as a permission graph, not individual rules.

item.title: MeshCore Brazil: Decentralized Communication Without Infrastructure
item.description: How LoRa radios and mesh networking enable community-driven communication over dozens of kilometers — without internet, cellular, or any centralized provider.

item.title: The "Misantropia" Incident: Brazil's National Alert System Failure
item.description: How a teenager with five-year-old leaked credentials shut down Brazil's national emergency alert system — and what the exposed debug mode, SQL injection, and missing MFA say about critical public infrastructure security.

item.title: The Hidden Danger of Judging by Appearances
item.description: How appearance-based cognitive biases become the social engineer's preferred attack vector — and why trusting the "packaging" over evidence hands the attacker a map of your weakest point.
